```{=html}
<div class="teaching-demo" id="resistor-explorer" data-demo="resistor" role="region" aria-labelledby="resistor-demo-title">
  <div class="demo-heading"><div><p class="demo-eyebrow">Try it · Ohm's law in a circuit</p><h3 id="resistor-demo-title" class="unnumbered">Where does the voltage go?</h3></div><button type="button" data-fullscreen hidden>Enlarge demo</button></div>
  <p>Change the supply voltage and resistance. Then add an LED: some of the supply voltage now drops across the LED, leaving less across the resistor.</p>
  <div class="circuit-workbench">
    <div class="circuit-inputs">
      <div class="circuit-control"><label for="resistor-mode">Circuit</label><select id="resistor-mode"><option value="plain">Resistor only</option><option value="led">Resistor + LED</option></select></div>
      <div class="circuit-control"><label for="resistor-rating">Resistor power rating</label><select id="resistor-rating"><option value="0.125">⅛ W (125 mW)</option><option value="0.25" selected>¼ W (250 mW)</option><option value="0.5">½ W (500 mW)</option><option value="1">1 W</option></select></div>
      <div class="circuit-control"><label for="resistor-voltage">Supply voltage (V)</label><input id="resistor-voltage-number" type="number" aria-label="Supply voltage, volts" min="0" max="12" step="0.1" value="3.3"><input id="resistor-voltage" type="range" min="0" max="12" step="0.1" value="3.3"></div>
      <div class="circuit-control"><label for="resistor-resistance">Resistance (Ω)</label><input id="resistor-resistance-number" type="number" aria-label="Series resistance, ohms" min="0" max="2000" step="1" value="330"><input id="resistor-resistance" type="range" min="0" max="2000" step="1" value="330"></div>
      <div class="circuit-control" data-led-control hidden><label for="resistor-forward">LED forward drop (V)</label><input id="resistor-forward-number" type="number" aria-label="Model LED forward voltage drop, volts" min="1" max="4" step="0.05" value="2"><input id="resistor-forward" type="range" min="1" max="4" step="0.05" value="2"></div>
      <div class="circuit-control" data-led-control hidden><label for="resistor-limit">Example LED limit (mA)</label><input id="resistor-limit" type="number" min="1" max="100" step="1" value="20"><p class="circuit-hint">Use your LED's current rating.</p></div>
    </div>
    <div class="circuit-results">
      <dl class="demo-stats"><div><dt>Current</dt><dd id="resistor-current">10.000 mA</dd></div><div><dt>Resistor voltage</dt><dd id="resistor-drop">3.300 V</dd></div><div><dt>Resistor power</dt><dd id="resistor-power">33.000 mW</dd></div></dl>
      <figure class="circuit-figure"><svg id="resistor-circuit" viewBox="0 0 600 290" role="img" aria-labelledby="resistor-circuit-title resistor-circuit-description"><title id="resistor-circuit-title">Supply, resistor and optional LED</title><desc id="resistor-circuit-description">A 3.3 volt source drives 10 milliamps through a 330 ohm resistor.</desc><g class="circuit-wire"><path d="M130,112V65H220 M300,65H450 M450,250H130V168"></path><circle cx="130" cy="140" r="28"></circle><rect x="220" y="50" width="80" height="30" class="circuit-component"></rect><path id="resistor-bypass" d="M450,65V250"></path><path d="M310,220H230 M238,214L230,220L238,226"></path></g><text x="130" y="133" text-anchor="middle">+</text><text x="130" y="158" text-anchor="middle">−</text><text x="22" y="112">Supply</text><text id="resistor-source-label" x="22" y="139">3.3 V</text><text id="resistor-r-label" x="260" y="31" text-anchor="middle">R = 330 Ω</text><text id="resistor-drop-label" x="260" y="112" text-anchor="middle">VR = 3.300 V</text><text id="resistor-current-label" x="270" y="202" text-anchor="middle">10.000 mA</text><g id="resistor-led-symbol" hidden><g class="circuit-wire"><path d="M450,65V130 M430,170H470 M450,170V250"></path><path id="resistor-led-body" d="M430,130H470L450,170Z" fill="white"></path><path d="M478,133L500,111 M492,111H500V119 M486,152L508,130 M500,130H508V138"></path></g><text x="495" y="184">LED</text><text id="resistor-led-label" x="495" y="210">2.000 V</text></g></svg><figcaption id="resistor-circuit-caption">The whole supply voltage is across the resistor.</figcaption></figure>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="demo-presets" aria-label="Circuit examples"><button type="button" data-resistor-example="plain">3.3 V / 330 Ω</button><button type="button" data-resistor-example="led33">3.3 V + LED</button><button type="button" data-resistor-example="led10">10 V + same LED circuit</button></div>
  <p class="demo-formula" id="resistor-formula">I = 3.3 / 330 = 0.010 A; PR = I² × R = 0.033 W</p>
  <p id="resistor-status" class="circuit-status" role="status">Resistor power is below the selected 250 mW rating.</p>
  <details class="demo-explanation"><summary>How do I choose a resistor for an LED?</summary><p>In this simple model, resistor voltage = supply voltage − LED forward drop. For a chosen current, R = (Vsupply − Vf) / I, using amperes for I. For example, a 10 V supply, a 2 V LED drop and a 10 mA target give R = 8 / 0.010 = 800 Ω. A nearby 820 Ω resistor gives slightly less current. Check resistor power with PR = I²R.</p><p>When the supply is at or below the selected LED drop, this model gives zero forward current. At zero resistance, it cannot calculate a finite current. Real LEDs have a curved current–voltage relationship rather than a fixed drop.</p></details>
  <p class="demo-note">An ideal bench-supply model. The LED limit and resistor rating are editable examples; this does not model GPIO drive limits, component tolerances or temperature.</p>
  <div class="demo-footer"><p><strong>Try:</strong> In resistor-only mode, double the voltage. Does resistor power double too? Then find a resistance for about 10 mA in the 10 V LED circuit.</p><button type="button" data-reset>Reset</button></div>
  <noscript><p>Enable JavaScript to use the controls. A 3.3 V supply across 330 Ω gives 10 mA and 33 mW. Doubling the voltage doubles current and quadruples resistor power.</p></noscript>
</div>
```
